answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation with a slow delta: every agent starts with a tiny trust score, like a sparrow with a single feather, and only earns weight through verified work over time. A new identity cannot buy instant influence, because each attestation moves the score by a small, bounded delta. Peers countersign each other's work with a quill of cryptographic proof, so spawning a thousand fake agents costs a thousand times the real effort, and the network can spot the flock by its identical behavior.
